driver: the GLP-1 DRUG VALUE CHAIN's SECOND GROWTH PHASE — incretin therapy transitioning from supply-constrained scarcity to a volume-driven, price-competitive, chronic-treatment market: affordability/access expansion, resolution of supply constraints, oral formulations, direct-to-patient distribution, generic/compounded entry, and an induction-to-maintenance chronic model. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.

disclosed_facts.fact: MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide) is disclosed as a differentiated antibody-peptide conjugate that activates the GLP-1 receptor and antagonizes GIPR; in March 2025 Amgen initiated two global Phase 3 studies in chronic weight management (one in adults with obesity/overweight without Type 2 diabetes, one with Type 2 diabetes).

By November 2025, four additional global Phase 3 MariTide studies were underway — in established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with obesity/overweight, heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction with obesity, and two in obstructive sleep apnea (on and not on positive airway pressure therapy) with obesity/overweight — for a total of six disclosed Phase 3 programs.

January 2026: Part 2 of the Phase 2 chronic weight management study (an additional 52 weeks in people who lost ≥15% body weight in Part 1) completed — the large majority of participants maintained Part 1 weight loss on a LOWER MONTHLY DOSE or QUARTERLY DOSE, with very low incidence of nausea/vomiting, no new safety signals, and sustained cardiometabolic improvements — i.e., disclosed clinical support for an induction-to-maintenance chronic dosing model.

January 2026: a Phase 2 study of MariTide in Type 2 diabetes (in adults living with and without obesity) completed its 24-week timepoint, showing clinically meaningful HbA1c and weight reductions with monthly dosing and a tolerability profile consistent with the GLP-1 class (predominantly mild-to-moderate GI events during dose escalation).

June 2025: underlying details from Part 1 of the MariTide Phase 2 study and complete primary-analysis results from the Phase 1 pharmacokinetics low-dose-initiation (PK-LDI) study evaluating lower starting doses were presented at the American Diabetes Association 85th Scientific Sessions and published in The New England Journal of Medicine — disclosed work on dose-initiation/tolerability, a stated element of the differentiated profile.

Amgen operates in one operating segment (human therapeutics) and reports total revenues of $10,054M for Q2 2026 and $18,672M for the six months ended June 30, 2026, with product sales of $9,537M and $17,755M respectively — no incretin/obesity product revenue is disclosed; MariTide is a candidate, not a marketed product, in the filings provided.

R&D expense rose to $1,868M in Q2 2026 (from $1,744M) and $3,587M for the six months (from $3,230M), disclosed at the consolidated level only, with defined R&D categories including 'Later-Stage Clinical Programs' (phase 2/3 programs intended to result in registration) — no MariTide-specific spend is broken out.

The filings disclose U.S. drug-pricing/affordability pressure applicable to Amgen generally — the Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing Executive Order (May 12, 2025), the July 31, 2025 MFN Letter sent to manufacturers including Amgen, the IRA, PDABs, PBMs, the 340B Program and (in the 10-Q) a 'GENEROUS' (GENErating cost Reductions fOr U.S. Medicaid) defined term — with no incretin-specific pricing economics disclosed.

Amgen discloses its own manufacturing, distribution and raw materials operations and a portfolio of delivery devices/autoinjectors (SureClick, AutoTouch, ConfiPen, ENBREL Mini, Onpro) — disclosed for its existing biologics portfolio, with no incretin/peptide API, fill-finish or device capacity attributed to GLP-1 products.

The structure is PARALLEL categories: (1) incumbent-franchise — marketed incretin franchises (two-sided: volume tailwind AND price/share headwind); (2) next-gen-assets — differentiated pipelines (orals, amylin, multi-agonists, muscle-preserving combinations); (3) manufacturing-infra — peptide API, CDMO / fill-finish capacity, devices/auto-injectors (the infrastructure-economics leg); (4) access-distribution — direct-to-patient, pharmacy/telehealth fulfillment, and generic distribution WITH disclosed incretin volume linkage. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.

disclosed_facts.fact: 10-K states that with respect to GLP-1 medications, during fiscal 2026 the company experienced increased demand which positively impacted Pharma segment revenue and consolidated revenue; however, increased GLP-1 sales did not meaningfully contribute to segment profit.

Pharma (Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions) segment revenue rose 15% to $234.8 billion in fiscal 2026, attributed to branded and specialty pharmaceutical sales growth from existing and new customers; total revenue up 14% to $254.2 billion — the segment through which the disclosed GLP-1 demand flows, but with no GLP-1 amount broken out.

Q3 FY26 10-Q attributes revenue growth of 11% to $60.9 billion (quarter) and 17% to $190.6 billion (nine months) primarily to branded and specialty pharmaceutical sales growth from existing customers, with no GLP-1 attribution or volume linkage disclosed.

10-K describes the Pharma segment generics program (generic product launches, customer volumes, pricing changes, the Red Oak Sourcing venture with CVS Health, and generic contract manufacturing/sourcing costs) as a positive driver of segment profit — generic distribution capability, but with no disclosed incretin/GLP-1 volume linkage.

10-K discloses branded-pharmaceutical policy exposure: the Inflation Reduction Act price caps have adversely impacted revenue (without negatively impacting profitability), and the Most-Favored-Nation drug pricing Executive Order and other administrative actions may affect sales or profitability of branded pharmaceutical products — a pricing-compression channel disclosed at the branded-pharma level, not attributed to incretins.

10-K discloses an April 2026 presidential proclamation imposing tariffs on imported branded pharmaceutical products and associated ingredients, which could raise costs or cause supply disruptions if manufacturers raise prices or stop importing; statements also indicate generics could face 100% tariffs in 2028 and 200% in 2029 — supply/cost risk disclosed generally, not tied to incretin products.

10-K discloses the acquisition of Advanced Diabetes Supply Group (ADS) contributing to Other segment revenue growth of 26% to $6.8 billion (with at-Home Solutions, Nuclear and Precision Health Solutions, OptiFreight Logistics) — diabetes-adjacent direct-to-patient supply distribution, with no disclosed GLP-1/incretin volume or revenue linkage.

disclosed_facts.fact: Corcept describes itself as a commercial-stage company discovering and developing cortisol-modulating medications for severe endocrinologic, oncologic, metabolic and neurologic disorders; marketed products are Korlym (mifepristone) and an authorized generic of Korlym for hypercortisolism (Cushing's syndrome). No incretin/GLP-1 product, program, API, CDMO or distribution activity is disclosed anywhere in the filing stream.

CATALYST study in patients with difficult-to-control diabetes (HbA1c 7.5%+ despite optimum treatment): 23.8% of 1,057 enrolled patients had hypercortisolism; in the randomized second phase Korlym produced a 1.47% HbA1c reduction vs 0.15% placebo, plus secondary-endpoint reductions in body weight (5.1 kg) and waist circumference (5.1 cm) vs placebo. This is cortisol modulation in diabetes/metabolic patients, not an incretin/GLP-1 asset; no GLP-1 combination, comparison or co-administration program is disclosed.

Relacorilant pipeline disclosures: NDA for endogenous hypercortisolism received an FDA Complete Response Letter on December 30, 2025 and was resubmitted June 17, 2026; FDA approved Lifyorli (relacorilant) with nab-paclitaxel in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer on March 25, 2026. Trials reported improvements in hypertension, glucose control, weight and body composition — a selective glucocorticoid-receptor modulator, not an incretin, amylin, multi-agonist or oral GLP-1 asset.

Additional programs disclosed: cortisol modulation for solid tumors (ovarian, endometrial, cervical, pancreatic, prostate), ALS, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)/fatty liver disease. MASH is metabolic but disclosed as a cortisol-modulation mechanism; no incretin/GLP-1 linkage is disclosed.

Product revenue, net of $256.1 million for Q2 2026 and $421.1 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 is entirely from Korlym and its authorized generic (hypercortisolism); no GLP-1/incretin revenue component is disclosed or broken out.

Distribution arrangements disclosed are specialty-pharmacy services for Korlym: exclusive vendor Optime Care terminated effective January 8, 2026, with substantially all specialty pharmacy services transferred to Curant Health Georgia, LLC in Q4 2025. This is single-product specialty pharmacy fulfillment with no disclosed incretin/GLP-1 volume linkage.

The structure is PARALLEL categories: (1) incumbent-franchise — marketed incretin franchises (two-sided: volume tailwind AND price/share headwind); (2) next-gen-assets — differentiated pipelines (orals, amylin, multi-agonists, muscle-preserving combinations); (3) manufacturing-infra — peptide API, CDMO / fill-finish capacity, devices/auto-injectors (the infrastructure-economics leg); (4) access-distribution — direct-to-patient, pharmacy/telehealth fulfillment, and generic distribution WITH disclosed incretin volume linkage. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.

disclosed_facts.fact: Lead product candidate pemvidutide (formerly ALT-801) is a balanced 1:1 glucagon/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist in clinical development for MASH, alcohol use disorder (AUD) and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD); the company describes itself as a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapies for serious liver diseases and states it is heavily dependent on pemvidutide's success.

Pemvidutide is disclosed as a multi-agonist incretin-class asset with muscle-preserving differentiation: the MOMENTUM Phase 2 trial in overweight and obese participants showed significant weight loss characterized by relative sparing of lean muscle mass and improvements in serum lipids; the company states pemvidutide has shown clinically meaningful weight loss with 'class-leading lean mass preservation.'

As of December 31, 2025, over 700 patients had been exposed to pemvidutide across 8 completed and 2 ongoing studies; pemvidutide received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for MASH based on 24-week data from the biopsy-driven IMPACT Phase 2b trial, and has demonstrated reductions in liver fat, liver inflammation markers, early MASH resolution and improvements in non-invasive tests (ELF score, Liver Stiffness Measurement).

10-Q reiterates pemvidutide as the lead candidate (balanced 1:1 glucagon/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist for MASH, AUD, ALD) and that the company may pursue additional indications leveraging its differentiated clinical profile; the company remains pre-revenue, reporting $0 revenue for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 (versus $5K and $10K in the prior-year periods) and a $45.4 million net loss for the six months, with R&D expense of $34.8 million.

disclosed_facts.fact: Obesity program: in June 2025 the company nominated PN-477, described as a potential best-in-class novel triple GLP-1/GIP/GCG receptor agonist peptide with both oral (PN-477o) and subcutaneous (PN-477sc) routes, as a development candidate for obesity; designed for total body weight loss, improved GI tolerability and improved fat-to-lean mass ratio with once-daily oral dosing and once-weekly SC optionality. IND-enabling studies are underway, with Phase 1 initiation anticipated by mid-2026 (PN-477sc) and 2H 2026 (PN-477o).

Second obesity development candidate: in December 2025 the company nominated PN-458, a potential best-in-class novel dual GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist peptide, for obesity, with optionality for oral (PN-458o) and subcutaneous (PN-458sc) formulations; IND-enabling studies for both are ongoing.

Company describes itself as an integrated peptide discovery and development company whose programs span three therapeutic areas including metabolic diseases, using a proprietary de novo peptide discovery platform (the platform from which the oral GLP-1-class candidates are derived).

Metabolic diseases remains one of three stated therapeutic areas in the most recent quarterly filing; the company is described as a discovery through late-stage development biopharmaceutical company with a proprietary peptide discovery platform.

All disclosed license and collaboration revenue derives from non-incretin assets: Icotyde (icotrokinra, oral IL-23R peptide licensed to JNJ; U.S. approval March 2026) and rusfertide (hepcidin mimetic for polycythemia vera, partnered with Takeda). Reported license and collaboration revenue of $213.5 million for Q2 2026 and $269.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 is attributable to these programs, not to any GLP-1 asset.

Company states it has no approved products generating commercial product revenue historically and has never generated revenue from product sales; it relies on third-party contract manufacturers for drug substance and clinical drug product (no disclosed incretin manufacturing capacity of its own).

Balance sheet at June 30, 2026 shows $420.1 million cash and equivalents plus $429.4 million marketable securities ($362.5M current, $66.9M non-current), funding R&D of $88.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 across all programs including the obesity candidates (no obesity-specific spend broken out).

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.

Revenue attributable to linaclotide partnerships comprised substantially all revenue; no GLP-1/incretin revenue disclosed.

Pricing/access dynamics disclosed relate to LINZESS, not incretins: HHS released a Maximum Fair Price of $136 per 30-day equivalent supply effective January 1, 2027 under the Inflation Reduction Act, and effective January 1, 2026 the Company and AbbVie lowered the LINZESS list price.

disclosed_facts.fact: Company describes itself as a late-stage rare disease company focused on hypoglycemia caused by hyperinsulinism (HI); lead asset ersodetug is an IV human monoclonal antibody that binds an allosteric site on the insulin receptor to down-modulate insulin signaling — an anti-insulin-receptor mechanism, not an incretin/GLP-1 agonist. No mention of GLP-1, incretin, semaglutide/tirzepatide, obesity or weight management anywhere in the filings.

Pipeline activity disclosed is entirely in ultra-rare hypoglycemia indications: completed enrollment (May 2025) of the pivotal Phase 3 sunRIZE study of ersodetug in congenital HI (~56 participants, >12 countries), with orphan drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, PRIME, ILAP and FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations; addressable congenital HI market estimated at more than 1,500 U.S. individuals.

Second program is the Phase 3 registrational upLIFT single-arm open-label study of ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism (insulinomas/non-islet cell tumors), initiated mid-2025 with as few as 16 participants after an August 19, 2025 FDA meeting removed the placebo-controlled requirement; immediately addressable market estimated at ~1,500 U.S. patients. No incretin/GLP-1 linkage disclosed.

Financial statements show no product or collaboration revenue of any kind — nine months ended March 31, 2026 report only operating expenses (R&D $38.9M, G&A $22.5M), a net loss of $57.1M, and cash/investments of $11.2M cash plus $109.0M marketable securities; therefore no revenue attributable to any GLP-1 value-chain category.

Recent 8-K disclosures relate exclusively to the hyperinsulinism programs: interim upLIFT update (June 2, 2026), Phase 3 sunRIZE oral presentation results (May 1, 2026), FDA meeting results (March 24, 2026), and sunRIZE insights plus expanded-access-program data on the initial 9 tumor HI participants (January 7, 2026) — none referencing incretin therapy, oral GLP-1 formulations, peptide manufacturing, or direct-to-patient distribution.

Company states future dependence on third-party manufacturers or strategic partners to manufacture any approved pharmaceutical drugs — i.e., it owns no peptide API, CDMO or fill-finish capacity of its own; no manufacturing infrastructure exposure disclosed.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.

disclosed_facts.fact: Lead investigational asset avexitide is described as a first-in-class GLP-1 receptor ANTAGONIST, designed to bind the GLP-1 receptor on pancreatic beta cells and inhibit the effect of GLP-1 to mitigate hypoglycemia; developed for post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH) and congenital hyperinsulinism, with FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation in both, Rare Pediatric Disease Designation in Congenital HI, and Orphan Drug Designation for hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

Phase 3 LUCIDITY trial of avexitide in PBH after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: ~75 participants at 21 U.S. sites, 3:2 randomization to 90 mg subcutaneous once daily vs placebo, 16-week double-blind period plus 32-week open-label extension; recruitment complete, last patients to be randomized/dosed Q1 2026, topline expected Q3 2026, potential commercial launch in 2027.

Prior avexitide clinical data cited across five trials in PBH, including Phase 2 PREVENT (n=18) where mean plasma glucose nadir increased 21% (p=0.001) and 26% (p=0.0002) vs placebo, and an open-label Phase 2b (n=16) where 90 mg once daily produced statistically significant 53% reduction in Level 2 (p=0.004) and 66% reduction in Level 3 (p=0.0003) hypoglycemic events.

Target patient population disclosed as PBH, estimated to affect approximately 8% of U.S. patients who have undergone sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (approximately 160,000 people in the U.S.), a condition thought to be caused by an excessive GLP-1 response leading to hypoglycemia; no approved therapies exist.

Preclinical program AMX0318 in PBH (and other rare diseases) is in IND-enabling studies; company describes itself as advancing programs in endocrine conditions alongside neurodegenerative diseases (AMX0035 in Wolfram syndrome, AMX0114 in ALS).

August 19, 2026 underwritten equity offering of 14,090,000 shares at $35.50 per share (plus 30-day option for 2,113,500 additional shares), net proceeds of approximately $471.7 million (up to ~$542.5 million if option exercised), which the Company intends to use together with existing cash to fund the potential U.S. commercial launch of avexitide, if approved.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.
